reason: Section 117.1 separates offences for violating regulations from offences and punishment categories for Act provisions listed in Schedule A.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offences for violating or failing to comply with regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 117.1(1) and 117.1(2) deal with regulation violations and whether the offence is category B or a prescribed category.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how violations of the regulations become offences and how their offence category is determined.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Schedule A Act offences and punishment categories
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 117.1(3) and 117.1(4) make listed Act provisions offences and tie their punishment categories to Schedule A.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Schedule A identifies Act offences and their Provincial Offences Procedure Act categories.

reason: Section 118 is one continuing-offence fine rule multiplying both minimum and maximum fines by the number of days the offence continues.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fine calculation for continuing offences

evidenceText: multiplied by the number of days

proposedGroups.reason: The target states how fines are calculated when an offence continues for more than one day.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how minimum and maximum fines are calculated for continuing offences.

reason: Section 119 is one corporate-party offence rule for officers, directors, employees or agents who direct, authorize, assent to, acquiesce in or participate in a corporate offence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officers, directors, employees and agents as parties to corporate offences

evidenceText: directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated
whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies when individuals connected to a corporation are parties to the corporation’s offence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a corporation’s officer, director, employee or agent is a party to an offence committed by the corporation.

reason: Section 120 is a short liability-preservation rule stating that section 119 does not relieve the offending corporation from liability.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporation remains liable despite individual party liability

evidenceText: Nothing in section 119 relieves the corporation

proposedGroups.reason: The target depends on section 119 but independently states that corporate liability remains.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that individual party liability under section 119 does not relieve the corporation from liability.

reason: Section 121 is one attribution rule treating acts, omissions, neglect or failures of corporate officers, directors, employees or agents acting within scope as those of the corporation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Attribution of corporate agents’ acts and omissions to corporation

evidenceText: is the act, omission, neglect or failure of the corporation

proposedGroups.reason: The target states when conduct of corporate personnel is construed as conduct of the corporation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an officer, director, employee or agent’s act, omission, neglect or failure is treated as the corporation’s.

reason: Section 122 is a coherent evidentiary rule for a Recorder certificate, including admissibility, notice to the opposing party and possible cross-examination.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder certificate evidence, notice and cross-examination
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together address prima facie proof by certificate, pre-trial notice and requiring the Recorder’s attendance for cross-examination.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a Recorder certificate may be used as evidence and what notice and cross-examination rights apply.

reason: Section 123 separates the continuation or recording of previous-Act mining claims from special work, fee and excess-work credit treatment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Previous-Act mining claims deemed or recorded as mineral claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 123(1) and 123(2) state how recorded and staked-but-unrecorded claims under the previous Act become mineral claims under this Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mining claims under the previous Act continue or may be recorded as mineral claims under this Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Work, fee and excess-work credits for previous-Act claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 123(3) and 123(4) preserve previous-Act work and fee rules for the term in progress and deem excess work credited with a tenth-term limit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how work requirements, fees in lieu of work and excess-work credits are treated for previous-Act mining claims.

reason: Section 124 is too broad for one unit because it covers continuation of previous-Act mining licences, conversion choices into leases or mineral claims, and credit, replacement and expiry consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation and limited renewal of previous-Act mining licences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 124(1) continues certain mining licences under the previous Act, applies previous-Act licence provisions and limits renewals to two one-year terms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act mining licences continue and how their renewal is limited.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Applying for mining leases or staking mineral claims before licence expiry
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 124(2) to 124(4.1) address the holder’s options or duties to apply for a mining lease, stake and record claims, and treat coal rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lease-application, claim-staking and coal-right options or duties before a continued mining licence expires.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Credits, replacement, expiry and excess-work consequences for continued licences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 124(5) to 124(9) cover work credits, replacement of the old licence, expiry consequences, coal withdrawal, deemed fifth term and excess-work carry-forward.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the work-credit, replacement, expiry, coal-withdrawal, term and excess-work consequences for continued mining licences.

reason: Section 125 is a focused saving rule continuing previous-Act mining leases and applying new-Act rent and required-work rules after renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation and renewal consequences for previous-Act mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how previous-Act mining leases continue and what rent and required-work rules apply after renewal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act mining leases continue and what rent and required-work rules apply after renewal.

reason: Section 126 is a coherent saving rule for withdrawn land and agreements, deeming previous-Act withdrawals and arrangements to continue under section 25 of this Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Previous-Act withdrawn lands and agreements deemed under section 25
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address land withdrawn under prior law and agreements, licences or leases that continue and are deemed under section 25.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act withdrawn lands and related agreements, licences or leases continue under this Act.

reason: Section 127 is one transition rule deeming a previous-Act prospecting licence to be issued under this Act, while setting its expiry at the next October 31.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Previous-Act prospecting licences deemed valid under this Act

evidenceText: deemed to be a prospecting licence issued under this Act
expires at midnight on the thirty-first day of October

proposedGroups.reason: The target states the continued validity and expiry rule for previous-Act prospecting licences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a previous-Act prospecting licence continues and when it expires.

reason: Section 128 is one transitional recalculation rule for excess work credited under the previous Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recalculation of accumulated excess work under previous Act

evidenceText: recalculated at a rate of five dollars for each day

proposedGroups.reason: The target states the rate for recalculating excess work credited under the previous Act at commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how excess work credited under the previous Act is recalculated.

reason: Section 128.1 separates the revocation and payment consequences for the Mining Commissioner from the immunity from proceedings arising from the revocation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Revocation of Mining Commissioner appointment and payment consequences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 128.1(1) to 128.1(3) revoke the appointment, nullify related contracts, agreements or orders and bar remuneration or expenses.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the appointment, contract and payment consequences of revoking the Mining Commissioner appointment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No proceedings from Mining Commissioner appointment revocation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 128.1(4) bars actions, applications or proceedings against listed Ministers or the Crown resulting from the revocation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the protection from proceedings arising from revocation of the Mining Commissioner appointment.

reason: Section 128.2 is one reference-conversion rule reading references to the Mining Commissioner in other instruments as references to the Board unless context requires otherwise.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: References to Mining Commissioner read as Board

evidenceText: shall be read as a reference to the Board

proposedGroups.reason: The target states how references to the Mining Commissioner are read after transition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when references to the Mining Commissioner are read as references to the Board.

reason: Section 128.3 is one continuation rule preserving valid Mining Commissioner decisions or orders and deeming them Board decisions or orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation and deeming of Mining Commissioner decisions

evidenceText: deemed to be a decision or order of the Board

proposedGroups.reason: The target preserves pre-commencement decisions or orders and deems them Board decisions or orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how valid Mining Commissioner decisions or orders continue after the appointment is revoked.

reason: Section 128.4 separates pending applications handled by the revoked Mining Commissioner under old law from the Minister’s ability to direct the Board to deal with such applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining Commissioner handling of pre-commencement applications
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 128.4(1) to 128.4(4) assign pre-commencement applications to the Mining Commissioner, require old law, provide compensation and deem resulting orders, decisions or actions to be Board actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how applications filed before commencement are handled by the revoked Mining Commissioner and how resulting decisions are treated.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister direction for Board to handle pre-commencement applications
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 128.4(5) separately authorizes the Minister to direct the Board to deal with an application referred to in subsection (1).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may direct the Board to deal with a pre-commencement application.

reason: Section 128.5 separates hearings held or completed by the revoked Mining Commissioner from the Minister-directed Board hearing path and its procedure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining Commissioner holding or completing pre-commencement hearings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 128.5(1) to 128.5(5) require the Mining Commissioner to hold or complete specified hearings under old law, provide compensation and deem decisions, orders or actions to be Board actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how pre-commencement hearings are held or completed by the revoked Mining Commissioner and how their results are treated.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister direction for Board to hold or complete hearings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 128.5(6) and 128.5(7) separately allow Minister direction to the Board and require Board hearing procedures for those hearings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may direct the Board to hold or complete a hearing and which procedures apply.

reason: Section 128.6 is a focused records-transfer rule transferring Mining Commissioner records to the Board in final-decision, Board-directed application and Board-directed hearing situations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transfer of Mining Commissioner records to the Board
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify the records transferred on commencement and when the Minister directs the Board to deal with applications or hearings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when records of the Mining Commissioner are transferred to the Board.
